examples.en: I felt sympathy after hearing that story.
I helped him out of sympathy.

examples.ko: 아이들은 길 잃은 강아지에게 동정심을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: The children felt pity for the lost puppy.

examples.ko: 뉴스를 보면 동정심 많은 사람들이 기부를 해요.
examples.en: On the news, compassionate people make donations.
Sympathy alone can't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 나는 그 사람에게 동정심이 하나도 안 들어요.
examples.en: I don't feel any sympathy for that person.

explain: '동정심이 생기다/들다', '동정심을 느끼다'처럼 써요. 불쌍하게 여기는 마음이라서 상대가 자기를 낮춰 본다고 느낄 수 있어서 '동정하지 마세요'라고 싫어하는 사람도 있어요. 더 깊고 따뜻한 마음은 '연민'이라고 하고, 글에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: You say '동정심이 생기다/들다' or '동정심을 느끼다'. Because it means feeling sorry for someone, the other person may feel looked down on, and some people say '동정하지 마세요' (don't pity me). '연민' is a deeper, warmer feeling and is used more in writing.

examples.en: Soldiers found a tunnel in the mountains.
Moles live by digging burrows.
It was too dark and narrow inside the tunnel.
The kids play tunnel-digging in the sandbox.

examples.ko: 그 영화에는 땅굴로 탈출하는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: That movie has a scene of escaping through a tunnel.
They open a tunnel made long ago to tourists.

explain: '터널'은 차나 기차가 다니게 산이나 땅 밑을 뚫은 큰 길이고, '땅굴'은 사람이나 동물이 땅속에 파 놓은 굴이에요. '땅굴을 파다'로 자주 써요. 뉴스에서는 군사 이야기에 '땅굴'이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A '터널' is a large passage bored through a mountain or under the ground for cars and trains, while a '땅굴' is a hole dug into the ground by people or animals. You say '땅굴을 파다'. In the news, '땅굴' often appears in military stories.

examples.en: I kept cheering for my friend in my heart.
I let out everything that was on my mind.
I'm deeply grateful to my teacher.

examples.ko: 그 사람 얼굴이 아직도 맘속에 남아 있어요.
examples.en: That person's face is still lingering in my heart.

examples.ko: 맘속에 숨겨 둔 비밀이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: I have one secret hidden in my heart.
I was angry but kept it to myself.

explain: '마음속'을 줄인 말이라 말할 때 많이 써요. 글에서는 '마음속'이 더 자연스러워요. '맘속으로 생각하다/빌다', '맘속에 담아 두다'는 소리 내지 않고 속으로만 한다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '맘속' is a shortened form of '마음속' and is common in speech; in writing '마음속' is more natural. '맘속으로 생각하다/빌다' and '맘속에 담아 두다' carry the feeling of doing something silently, only inside.

en: stream of water; jet of water

examples.en: A stream of water pours down the mountain.
The water from the shower is too weak.
The firefighter sprayed a jet of water at the fire.
The course of this river runs all the way to the sea.
The sound of the waterfall is very loud.
The gardener sprays a thin stream of water on the flowers.

explain: 이름이 있는 큰 흐름은 '강'이고, 수도꼭지·호스·폭포에서 가늘고 길게 나오는 물에도 '물줄기'를 써요. '물줄기가 세다/약하다', '물줄기를 뿜다'처럼 말해요. 강이 흘러가는 길을 말할 때는 '물길'도 써요.
explain_en: A big named flow is a '강', but '물줄기' is also used for the thin, long line of water from a faucet, a hose or a waterfall. You say '물줄기가 세다/약하다' and '물줄기를 뿜다'. For the path a river takes, '물길' is also used.

examples.en: Two kids bumped heads while running.

examples.ko: 축구 선수가 상대에게 박치기를 해서 퇴장당했어요.
examples.en: The soccer player head-butted an opponent and was sent off.
A head-butt is a foul in wrestling.

examples.ko: 동생이 갑자기 내 배를 박치기로 들이받았어요.
examples.en: My little brother suddenly head-butted my stomach.
We almost bumped heads in front of the door.
The baby bumped his head on the corner of the bed while playing.

explain: '박치기하다'로 동사처럼도 써요. 일부러 머리로 들이받을 때뿐 아니라 실수로 머리끼리 부딪칠 때도 써요. 사고 상황을 말할 때는 '머리를 부딪치다'가 더 차분한 말이고, '박치기'는 어린이 말투 같은 가벼운 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It is also used as a verb, '박치기하다'. It covers deliberate head-butts and accidental head bumps. For an accident, '머리를 부딪치다' sounds calmer; '박치기' has a light, childlike feel.

examples.en: It's a sheer curtain, so some light comes in.

examples.ko: 이 비닐봉지는 반투명해서 안이 흐릿하게 보여요.
examples.en: This plastic bag is translucent, so the inside looks blurry.
The bathroom glass is frosted.
I put the snacks in a translucent plastic container.
I put a translucent film on the new window.
The ice turned translucent as it melted.

explain: '투명'은 뒤까지 다 보이고, '반투명'은 빛은 통하지만 모양이 흐릿하게 보여요. 반대말은 '불투명'이에요. '반투명 유리'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙이거나 '반투명하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '투명' lets you see through completely, while '반투명' lets light through but the shapes look blurry. The opposite is '불투명'. It is used before another noun, as in '반투명 유리', or as '반투명하다'.

examples.en: The police went out wearing body armor.
Reporters also wear body armor on battlefields.

examples.ko: 방탄복이 너무 무거워서 오래 입기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The vest is so heavy that it's hard to wear for long.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 방탄복 덕분에 살아났어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie survived thanks to a bulletproof vest.

examples.ko: 새 방탄복을 사려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Buying a new bulletproof vest costs a lot.
When I took off the vest, sweat poured down.

explain: '방탄'은 총알을 막는다는 뜻이라 '방탄유리', '방탄조끼'에도 붙어요. 몸통만 덮는 조끼 모양은 '방탄조끼'라고도 많이 불러요.
explain_en: '방탄' means stopping bullets, so it is also used in '방탄유리' (bulletproof glass) and '방탄조끼' (bulletproof vest). A vest that covers only the torso is often called '방탄조끼'.

examples.en: This tumbler keeps heat well.
In winter you need to pay attention to keeping warm.
I put hot soup in an insulated lunch box.
I bought long underwear with a good warming effect.

examples.ko: 아기 방은 보온을 위해 창문에 뽁뽁이를 붙였어요.
examples.en: For warmth, I put bubble wrap on the baby room's window.

examples.ko: 엄마가 보온병에 차를 가득 담아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom filled a thermos with tea for me.

explain: 따뜻함을 지킨다는 말이라서 차갑게 지키는 '보냉'과 짝이에요. '보온병', '보온 도시락', '보온 효과'처럼 뒤에 다른 말을 붙일 때가 많고 '보온이 잘 되다'로 써요.
explain_en: '보온' is about keeping heat in, and its pair is '보냉', keeping things cold. It is often followed by another word, as in '보온병', '보온 도시락' and '보온 효과', and you say '보온이 잘 되다'.

examples.ko: 친구가 떠난 뒤 큰 상실감을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a deep sense of loss after my friend left.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 일하던 회사를 나오니 상실감이 컸어요.
examples.en: Leaving the company I'd worked at for years left me with a big sense of loss.

examples.ko: 상실감 때문에 아무것도 하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of this sense of loss, I don't want to do anything.
He went on a trip to soothe his sense of loss.

examples.ko: 이사하고 나서 이유 없는 상실감이 몰려왔어요.
examples.en: After I moved, a sense of loss came over me for no reason.
I comforted my friend who was sunk in a sense of loss.

explain: 물건보다 사람, 꿈, 자리처럼 마음에 큰 것을 잃었을 때 써요. '상실감을 느끼다/겪다', '상실감이 크다'로 말해요. 가벼운 물건을 잃었을 때는 '아쉽다', '허전하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '-감'은 느낌을 뜻해서 '안도감', '성취감'과 같은 틀이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you lose something big to the heart, such as a person, a dream or a position, more than an object. You say '상실감을 느끼다/겪다' and '상실감이 크다'. For losing something small, '아쉽다' or '허전하다' is more natural. '-감' means a feeling, as in '안도감' and '성취감'.

examples.en: I ate cotton candy at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 아이가 솜사탕을 보고 사 달라고 졸랐어요.
examples.en: The child saw the cotton candy and begged me to buy it.
Cotton candy melts quickly in your mouth.
The pink cotton candy looks like a cloud.

examples.ko: 시장 앞에서 아저씨가 솜사탕을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: A man is making cotton candy in front of the market.
My hands got sticky after eating cotton candy.

explain: '솜'과 '사탕'을 합친 이름이에요. 놀이공원이나 축제에서 먹는 간식이고 '솜사탕을 만들다/먹다'로 말해요. '솜사탕 같은 구름'처럼 폭신하고 달콤한 느낌을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: The name combines '솜' (cotton fluff) and '사탕' (candy). It is a snack from amusement parks and festivals; you say '솜사탕을 만들다/먹다'. It is also used figuratively, as in '솜사탕 같은 구름', for something soft, fluffy and sweet.

examples.en: A sense of relief washed over me when the exam ended.
I felt relieved at the news that the child was safe.
I feel secure when my family is by my side.
Hearing his voice gave me a sense of relief.

examples.ko: 큰 걱정이 사라져서 안도감에 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: My big worry disappeared, and I cried from relief.
This room strangely makes me feel at ease.

explain: '안도감을 느끼다/주다', '안도감이 들다'로 써요. 말로는 '다행이다', '마음이 놓이다'가 더 자주 나오고, '안도감'은 글이나 설명할 때 잘 써요. 반대로 불안한 마음은 '불안감'이에요.
explain_en: You say '안도감을 느끼다/주다' and '안도감이 들다'. In speech, '다행이다' and '마음이 놓이다' are more common; '안도감' fits writing and explanations better. The opposite feeling is '불안감'.

examples.en: The cat batted the toy with its front paw.
The puppy raises its front paw to say hello.
The horse raised its front legs and neighed loudly.
I went to the clinic to treat the injured front paw.
The bear caught a fish with its front paw.
Our dog scratches the door with its front paw.

explain: 짝말은 '뒷발'이에요. 동물에게는 '손' 대신 '앞발'을 쓰고, 다리 전체를 말할 때는 '앞다리'라고 해요. 개나 고양이가 앞발로 무엇을 하는지 말할 때 '앞발로 ~하다'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The paired word is '뒷발' (hind paw). For animals you say '앞발' instead of '손', and '앞다리' for the whole front leg. The pattern '앞발로 ~하다' often describes what a dog or cat does with its front paw.

examples.en: We keep potatoes in the underground storage room.
The temperature in this storehouse is always constant.
The food store is almost empty.

examples.ko: 농부들이 마을 저장고에 쌀을 쌓아 뒀어요.
examples.en: The farmers piled rice in the village storehouse.

examples.ko: 저장고 문을 열자 서늘한 공기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the storeroom door, cool air came out.
We saved money to build a new storehouse.

explain: '창고'는 물건을 넣어 두는 건물 전체에 쓰고, '저장고'는 식량·물·에너지처럼 오래 모아 두는 것에 어울려요. 컴퓨터 자료를 두는 곳은 '저장소'나 '저장 공간'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '창고' covers any building for keeping goods, while '저장고' fits things stored for a long time, such as food, water or energy. For computer data, people say '저장소' or '저장 공간'.

examples.en: Right now I desperately need a rest.
He was in a situation where he badly needed money.
I earnestly hoped to pass.
At that moment I felt keenly how much I needed help.

examples.ko: 선생님이 해 주신 말이 절실히 와닿았어요.
examples.en: What my teacher said really hit home.

examples.ko: 난민들은 음식과 물을 절실히 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: The refugees are anxiously waiting for food and water.

explain: '필요하다', '바라다', '느끼다', '와닿다'와 잘 어울려요. '정말', '매우'보다 마음이 급하고 간절한 느낌이 강해요. 형용사 '절실하다'에서 온 부사예요.
explain_en: It pairs well with '필요하다', '바라다', '느끼다' and '와닿다'. It feels more urgent and heartfelt than '정말' or '매우'. It is the adverb form of the adjective '절실하다'.

examples.en: He is learning baking skills.

examples.ko: 제빵 학원에 다닌 지 석 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three months since I started going to a baking school.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 좋은 제빵 재료만 써요.
examples.en: This shop uses only good baking ingredients.

examples.ko: 제빵사가 되려면 어떤 공부를 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I need to study to become a baker?

examples.ko: 제빵 대회에서 우리 학교가 일등을 했어요.
examples.en: Our school took first place at the baking competition.
A nutty bread smell is coming from the bakery room.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '제빵 기술', '제빵사', '제빵 학원'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 과자와 케이크를 만드는 일은 '제과'라서 합쳐서 '제과제빵'이라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is rarely used alone; it usually takes a following word, as in '제빵 기술', '제빵사' and '제빵 학원'. Making cookies and cakes is '제과', so people often say '제과제빵' together.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 시장 지배력이 아주 커요.
examples.en: This company has great dominance in the market.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 바다에 대한 지배력을 잃었어요.
examples.en: That country lost its control over the sea.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 경기 후반에 지배력을 되찾았어요.
examples.en: Our team regained control in the second half of the game.

examples.ko: 지배력이 약해지자 부하들이 말을 안 들었어요.
examples.en: As his hold weakened, his subordinates stopped listening.

examples.ko: 큰 기업이 지배력을 이용해 가격을 올렸어요.
examples.en: The big company used its dominance to raise prices.

examples.ko: 주주 한 명이 회사에 대한 지배력을 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: One shareholder holds control over the company.

explain: '시장 지배력', '경영 지배력'처럼 경제나 정치 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '영향력'은 슬며시 변화를 주는 힘이고, '지배력'은 결정을 쥐고 통제하는 힘이라 더 세요. '지배력을 가지다/키우다/잃다'로 써요.
explain_en: It often appears in economics and politics, as in '시장 지배력' (market dominance) and '경영 지배력'. '영향력' is influence that gradually changes things, whereas '지배력' is the power to hold decisions and control, so it is stronger. You say '지배력을 가지다/키우다/잃다'.

examples.en: The curator planned this exhibition.
I looked at the paintings while listening to the curator.
I want to be a curator working at a museum.
A curator selects and arranges the works.
A young curator is in charge of this exhibition.
I went to the art museum to interview the curator.

explain: 공식 직책 이름은 '학예사'(학예연구사)지만 일상에서는 '큐레이터'를 더 많이 써요. 관람객에게 작품을 설명해 주는 '도슨트'와는 달라요. 큐레이터는 전시를 기획하고 도슨트는 안내해요.
explain_en: The official job title is '학예사' (학예연구사), but in daily life '큐레이터' is used more. A '도슨트' is different: a docent guides and explains works to visitors, while a curator plans the exhibition.

examples.en: There are many windmills in the Netherlands.
When the wind blew, the windmill turned slowly.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에 낡은 풍차가 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old windmill stands on the hill.
The child bought a windmill-shaped toy.

examples.ko: 여행 책에서 풍차 마을 사진을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a picture of a windmill village in a travel book.
Don Quixote mistook windmills for giants.

explain: 전기를 만드는 현대 기계는 '풍력 발전기'라고 하고, '풍차'는 옛날 곡식을 빻거나 물을 푸던 모양의 건물에 어울려요. 사진이나 동화 속 풍차 마을을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: A modern machine that makes electricity is a '풍력 발전기'; '풍차' fits the old-style structure used to grind grain or pump water. It is often used for windmill villages in photos and stories.

examples.ko: 매일 아침 학습지를 한 장씩 풀어요.
examples.en: Every morning I solve one sheet of the workbook.
The worksheet tutor comes to our house.
My younger brother hates the math worksheets.

examples.ko: 이번 달 학습지 값이 너무 비싸요.
examples.en: This month's workbook fee is too expensive.
I lost the worksheet I got as homework.

examples.ko: 학습지를 밀리면 나중에 한꺼번에 해야 해요.
examples.en: If you fall behind on worksheets, you have to do them all at once later.

explain: 한국에서는 집에서 매주 풀고 선생님이 확인해 주는 정기 교재를 '학습지'라고 많이 불러요. 서점에서 사서 푸는 책은 '문제집'이고, 학교에서 한 장씩 나눠 주는 종이는 '유인물'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: In Korea, a regular set of materials you solve at home weekly and a tutor checks is commonly called '학습지'. A book you buy at a bookstore to practice is a '문제집', and a sheet handed out at school is also called '유인물'.

examples.en: My older brother is learning hapkido.
At the hapkido dojang we practiced how to fall first.
Hapkido is a sport that uses the opponent's force.
I went to the gym to see a hapkido demonstration.
I go to hapkido class every weekend.
How are hapkido and taekwondo different?

explain: 한국에는 태권도, 합기도, 검도, 유도처럼 '-도'로 끝나는 무술 이름이 많아요. 합기도는 상대를 잡고 던지는 기술이 많아서 발차기가 중심인 태권도와 느낌이 달라요. '합기도를 하다/배우다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Many Korean martial arts end in '-도', such as 태권도, 합기도, 검도 and 유도. Hapkido has many grabbing and throwing techniques, so it feels different from taekwondo, which centers on kicks. You say '합기도를 하다/배우다'.

examples.en: Everyone hopes a nuclear war won't break out.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 핵전쟁 이후의 세상을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That movie shows the world after a nuclear war.
I watched a news report on the danger of nuclear war.

examples.ko: 핵전쟁이 나면 지구 전체가 위험해질 거예요.
examples.en: If a nuclear war breaks out, the whole Earth will be in danger.

examples.ko: 여러 나라가 핵전쟁을 막으려고 회담을 열었어요.
examples.en: Several countries held talks to prevent nuclear war.
In class we learned about the damage of nuclear war.

explain: '핵전쟁이 일어나다/나다', '핵전쟁을 막다/피하다'로 자주 써요. '핵'은 원자핵에서 온 말로 '핵무기', '핵발전소'에도 붙어요. 뉴스와 토론에서 주로 나오는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 가볍게 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Common patterns are '핵전쟁이 일어나다/나다' and '핵전쟁을 막다/피하다'. '핵' comes from the atomic nucleus and is also in '핵무기' and '핵발전소'. It mostly appears in news and debates, so it isn't used casually in everyday talk.

examples.en: My mother is going through menopause, so she often sweats.
During menopause, the body and mind change a lot.
She goes to the hospital because of menopause symptoms.
They say it gets much easier after menopause.
My wife is going through menopause and sleeps poorly.
They say men have it too.

explain: 주로 여성의 폐경 즈음을 말하지만 한국에서는 중년 남성에게도 '남성 갱년기'라고 해요. 중년이 되어 갑자기 예민해지거나 기운이 없을 때 '갱년기 왔나 봐'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. '갱년기가 오다/지나다/겪다'로 써요.
explain_en: It mainly refers to the period around a woman's menopause, but in Korea men in middle age are also said to have '남성 갱년기'. When someone suddenly gets irritable or low on energy in middle age, people joke '갱년기 왔나 봐'. You say '갱년기가 오다/지나다/겪다'.

examples.en: Seasoned bracken goes into bibimbap.
We pick bracken in the mountains in spring.
I boiled the bracken and left it soaking in water.
My grandmother sent me dried bracken.
Bracken is growing fast in the forest.
Seasoned bracken goes on the ancestral rites table.

explain: 한국에서는 말린 고사리를 물에 불려 삶아서 나물로 먹어요. 비빔밥과 육개장에 자주 들어가요. 반찬 이름으로는 '고사리나물'이라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 아이의 작고 통통한 손을 귀엽게 말할 때 써요. 어른의 손에는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used affectionately for a child's small, chubby hands. Not used for adult hands.

explain_en: In Korea, dried bracken is soaked in water, boiled and eaten as a seasoned vegetable side dish. It often goes into bibimbap and 육개장. As a side dish, it is called '고사리나물'.

examples.en: This monitor is high resolution, so the text is sharp.
Please send me a high-resolution photo.
High-resolution video takes up a lot of storage.
The new phone's screen changed to high resolution.
If you print in high resolution, the picture is cleaner.

examples.ko: 고해상도 이미지는 파일이 무거워서 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: High-resolution images are heavy files, so they take a long time.

explain: '저해상도'와 짝이에요. 말로는 '화질이 좋다', '선명하다'도 많이 써요. 'HD', '4K'처럼 이름이나 숫자로 말하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: The paired word is '저해상도'. In speech people also say '화질이 좋다' or '선명하다'. Names or numbers such as 'HD' and '4K' are also commonly used.

examples.en: Standing somewhere high, I was overcome by fear.
He has a great fear of the dark.
After the accident, I developed a fear of driving.

examples.ko: 아이에게 공포심을 주는 말은 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't say things that frighten a child.
My legs shook out of fear.
I took a deep breath to overcome my fear.

explain: '공포'는 무서운 상황이나 느낌이고 '공포심'은 마음속에 생기는 두려움에 초점이 있어요. '공포심을 느끼다/주다/이기다'로 써요. 가볍게 무서울 때는 '무섭다'를 쓰고, 영화나 소설 장르는 '공포 영화'처럼 '공포'를 써요.
explain_en: '공포' is a frightening situation or feeling, while '공포심' focuses on the fear that arises inside you. You say '공포심을 느끼다/주다/이기다'. For mild fear, use '무섭다'; for the genre of films or novels, use '공포', as in '공포 영화'.

examples.en: A distinguished guest is coming to today's event.
Those sitting in the VIP seats, please come this way.
The president attended as a guest of honor.

examples.ko: 호텔은 귀빈에게 가장 좋은 방을 줬어요.
examples.en: The hotel gave the best room to the VIP.
I was treated like a VIP, so I felt great.
Many distinguished guests gathered at the wedding.

explain: 공식 행사에서 높은 손님을 정중하게 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서 친구를 초대했을 때는 '귀빈'이 아니라 '손님'이라고 해요. 농담으로 '귀빈 대접을 받았다'고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This is a polite word for an important guest at an official event. When you invite a friend in daily life, you say '손님', not '귀빈'. People also use '귀빈 대접을 받았다' jokingly.

examples.en: Don't say such nonsense.
Don't fight with your friend over such a trivial thing.
Where are you going wearing clothes like that?
I won't fall for a lie like that.
With an attitude like that, it's hard to get a job.

examples.ko: 그따위 걱정은 하지 말고 푹 자요.
examples.en: Stop worrying about such things and get some sleep.

explain: 상대의 말이나 물건을 낮춰 보고 못마땅하게 말하는 표현이라서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 가까운 사이에서도 화난 느낌이 나요. 가까운 것은 '이따위', 먼 것은 '저따위'예요.
explain_en: It looks down on what the other person said or has and expresses disapproval, so you don't use it with elders or people you've just met. Even among close friends it sounds angry. A closer thing is '이따위' and a farther one is '저따위'.

examples.en: Ants find their way with their antennae.
The butterfly's antennae quivered.
The snail pulled its feelers right in.

examples.ko: 곤충 더듬이는 냄새를 맡는 일도 해요.
examples.en: Insect antennae also help them smell.
I found an insect with long antennae in the field guide.
The child closely observed the bug's antennae.

explain: 곤충이나 달팽이 머리에 달려 주변을 느끼는 부분에 써요. '더듬다'에서 온 말이라 손으로 더듬듯 주변을 살핀다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '더듬이가 길다/떨리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for the part on the head of an insect or snail that senses its surroundings. It comes from '더듬다' (to grope), giving the feel of probing around like a hand. It isn't used for people; you say '더듬이가 길다/떨리다'.

examples.en: I opened a shop with my friend as business partners.
Business partners split the profit half and half.
I'm worried because my partner and I disagree.
My longtime partner suddenly left the company.
We are partners who trust each other.

examples.ko: 동업자를 구할 때는 계약서를 꼭 써요.
examples.en: When you find a partner, be sure to write a contract.

explain: 함께 돈을 대고 일을 나누어 장사하는 사이에 써요. 월급을 받는 직원은 '동업자'가 아니고, 같은 직장 사람은 '동료'예요. 동사는 '동업하다'라서 '친구랑 동업하다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is for people who put in money together and share the work of a business. A salaried employee is not a '동업자', and someone at the same workplace is a '동료'. The verb is '동업하다', as in '친구랑 동업하다'.

examples.en: Please close the bottle cap tightly.
When I pulled the bathtub plug, the water drained.
The cap wouldn't open, so I popped it with a spoon.

examples.ko: 샴푸 마개를 열고 한 번 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I opened the shampoo cap and pressed once.
I sealed the bottle with a cork stopper.
There was no stopper, so all the water spilled.

explain: '뚜껑'은 위에서 덮는 것이고, '마개'는 구멍에 끼워 막는 것이에요. 그래서 '병마개'라고 하지만 냄비에는 '냄비 뚜껑'이라고 해요. '마개를 따다/열다/막다'로 써요.
explain_en: A '뚜껑' covers from the top, while a '마개' is pushed into an opening to block it. So it is '병마개', but for a pot it is '냄비 뚜껑'. You say '마개를 따다/열다/막다'.

examples.en: All the staff work wearing name tags.
The name tag has the name and grade written on it.
I got a new name tag for the new semester.
You can't enter without a name badge.
Please sew the name tag onto the uniform.
On the event day, we hang name tags around our necks.

explain: 가슴이나 목에 다는 이름표예요. '이름표'는 더 일상적이고, '명찰'은 회사·학교·군대처럼 공식적인 곳에서 자주 써요. '명찰을 달다/차다/걸다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a name tag worn on the chest or around the neck. '이름표' is more everyday, while '명찰' is used often in formal places like companies, schools and the military. You say '명찰을 달다/차다/걸다'.

en: unknown quantity; uncertain matter; up in the air

examples.en: Whether this business will succeed is still unknown.
The result is uncertain, but I'll do my best.

examples.ko: 그 팀이 우승할지는 아직 미지수라고 해요.
examples.en: They say it's still up in the air whether that team will win.

examples.ko: 미지수인 부분이 많아서 계획을 세우기 어려워요.
examples.en: There are many unknowns, so it's hard to make a plan.
In math, an unknown number is called an unknown.

examples.ko: 앞으로 이 회사가 어떻게 변할지 미지수예요.
examples.en: How this company will change in the future is anyone's guess.

explain: 수학에서는 x 같은 모르는 수를 '미지수'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '~는 아직 미지수예요'로 '어떻게 될지 모른다'는 뜻으로 자주 써요. 좋은지 나쁜지는 말하지 않고 불확실하다는 점만 말해서 부드러워요.
explain_en: In math, an unknown number like x is a '미지수'. In daily life, '~는 아직 미지수예요' means we can't tell how it will turn out. It says only that things are uncertain, not whether the outcome is good or bad, so it sounds soft.

examples.en: I read a book in front of the living room fireplace.
I put firewood in the fireplace.
I want to live in a house with a fireplace.

examples.ko: 눈 오는 날 벽난로 불빛이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: The fireplace light looks warm on a snowy day.

examples.ko: 아이들이 벽난로 앞에 모여 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: The kids gather in front of the fireplace and listen to a story.
Apartments these days almost never have a fireplace.

explain: 한국의 전통 집에는 온돌이 있어서 벽난로는 서양 영화나 펜션에서 더 자주 봐요. '벽난로에 불을 피우다', '벽난로 앞에 앉다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Traditional Korean houses have ondol floor heating, so fireplaces are more often seen in Western movies or pensions. You say '벽난로에 불을 피우다' and '벽난로 앞에 앉다'.

examples.en: The museum has a replica instead of the real one.
This painting is a reproduction, but it looks really similar.
I decided not to buy a knockoff bag.
A replica is much cheaper than the original.
The souvenir shop sells replicas of relics.
Please check whether this watch is a copy.

explain: 원래 것은 '원본'이나 '진품'이라고 해요. '복제품'은 똑같이 만든 것이라 박물관 유물 복제처럼 좋은 뜻으로도, 가짜 명품처럼 나쁜 뜻으로도 쓰여요. 나쁜 뜻은 '짝퉁'이라고도 하지만 짝퉁은 편한 말투예요.
explain_en: The original is a '원본' or '진품'. A '복제품' is a faithful copy, used positively for museum replicas and negatively for fake luxury goods. For the negative sense people also say '짝퉁', but that is casual.

examples.en: If dry grass catches fire, it spreads fast.
The matches are wet, so they don't light well.
The curtain caught fire and everyone was shocked.
The burning firewood crackles.
The competition between the two companies has heated up.
Ever since the debate got heated, the meeting has run long.

explain: '불이 붙다'가 더 흔하게 쓰이고, '불붙다'는 한 단어로 붙여 써요. 남이 불을 옮길 때는 '불을 붙이다'이고 '불붙다'는 저절로 붙는 쪽이에요. 경쟁이나 논쟁이 갑자기 뜨거워질 때도 '불붙다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 신제품 출시로 두 회사의 경쟁이 불붙었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 나는 것이 아니라 경쟁, 논쟁, 인기가 갑자기 뜨거워진다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not a real fire: a figure of speech for competition, debate or popularity suddenly getting intense.

explain_en: '불이 붙다' is the more common form; '불붙다' is written as one word. '불을 붙이다' is when someone sets something alight, while '불붙다' is it catching fire on its own. It is also used when a competition or debate suddenly heats up.

examples.en: The fishy smell fills the room.
I added ginger to get rid of the fishy smell.

examples.ko: 손에서 비린내가 나서 여러 번 씻었어요.
examples.en: My hands smelled fishy, so I washed them several times.

examples.ko: 이 생선은 비린내가 전혀 안 나요.
examples.en: This fish has no fishy smell at all.
As I entered the market, a fishy smell hit me.
If you sprinkle lemon juice, the fishy smell lessens.

explain: '비린내가 나다/풍기다', '비린내를 없애다/잡다'로 써요. 생선이나 날것에서 나는 냄새예요. 고기 쪽 냄새는 '누린내'라고 해요.
explain_en: You say '비린내가 나다/풍기다' and '비린내를 없애다/잡다'. It is the smell from fish or raw food. The smell of meat is called '누린내'.

examples.en: The upper floors of the building have offices.
In this apartment, the higher the floor, the better the view.

examples.ko: 비행기가 상층 기류 때문에 많이 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: The plane shook a lot because of upper-level air currents.

examples.ko: 불이 나자 상층 사람들이 먼저 대피했어요.
examples.en: When the fire broke out, the people on the upper floors evacuated first.

examples.ko: 그 파티에는 사회 상층 사람들만 모였어요.
examples.en: Only people from the upper class gathered at that party.

examples.ko: 바람이 센 날에는 상층 창문을 닫아 두세요.
examples.en: On windy days, keep the upper-floor windows closed.

explain: 아래쪽 '하층'과 짝이에요. 건물에서는 일상어로 '위층'을 많이 쓰고 '상층'은 설명 글에서 잘 써요. 사회에서 소득이나 지위를 나눌 때 '상층/중층/하층'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '하층' (lower layer). For buildings, '위층' is the everyday word and '상층' fits explanatory writing. It is also used to divide society by income or status into '상층/중층/하층'.

en: moment by moment; at every moment

examples.en: I want to do my best at every moment.
My mood changes from moment to moment, and it's hard.
I captured each moment of the trip in photos.
The child says amazing things every now and then.
I jot down thoughts as they come to me.
When driving, you have to stay focused at every moment.

explain: '순간'을 반복해서 '매 순간'이라는 뜻을 만들어요. '하루하루', '한 걸음 한 걸음'처럼 반복하면 하나씩 이어진다는 느낌이 생겨요. '순간순간 최선을 다하다'는 다짐할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: Repeating '순간' gives the sense of 'every single moment'. Repetitions like '하루하루' and '한 걸음 한 걸음' create a feeling of one-by-one continuity. '순간순간 최선을 다하다' is a common phrase for making a resolution.

examples.en: Seoul is the heart of Korea's politics and economy.
There is a big square at the heart of the city.
A spy got into the very core of the company.

examples.ko: 그 숲의 심장부에는 오래된 나무가 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old tree stands at the heart of that forest.
The engine is the heart of the machine.
This place is called the heart of the culture industry.

explain: 몸의 '심장'보다 '가장 중요한 중심 부분'을 비유할 때가 대부분이에요. 도시, 조직, 기계, 숲의 한가운데에 쓰고 '중심부'보다 힘이 모인 곳이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. 실제 심장의 위치는 보통 '심장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used far more often as a metaphor for the most important central part than for the body's '심장'. It applies to the middle of a city, organization, machine or forest, and feels stronger than '중심부', as the place where power gathers. The actual organ is usually just '심장'.

examples.en: You stayed up all night, so how are you so fresh?
My grandfather is still full of energy despite his age.
After drinking coffee, my mind felt sharp.

examples.ko: 아침에 푹 자고 일어나면 쌩쌩한 기분이에요.
examples.en: When I wake up after a good sleep, I feel fresh.
I took a nap, so I worked energetically in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝났는데도 친구는 쌩쌩하게 놀러 갔어요.
examples.en: Even after the exam, my friend went out to play, full of energy.

explain: 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 밤을 새웠는데 멀쩡할 때나 나이 든 분이 건강해 보일 때 써요. '팔팔하다'는 힘이 넘치고 활발한 느낌이고, '쌩쌩하다'는 지치지 않고 상태가 좋다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: This is a casual word for friends and family. You use it when someone is fine after staying up all night, or when an older person looks healthy. '팔팔하다' feels full of power and activity, while '쌩쌩하다' feels not worn out and in good shape.

examples.en: This tool has many uses.
I chose a bag to suit how I'd use it.
I decided to clear out things that have no use.
We learn how this word is used through example sentences.
I found a new use for the discarded bottle.
I write down where my money goes in a household ledger.

explain: '쓰임새가 많다/적다/있다/없다', '쓰임새를 찾다'처럼 써요. '용도'는 정해진 목적이고, '쓰임새'는 실제로 어디에 어떻게 쓰이는지를 말해서 더 쉽고 부드러워요. 돈의 쓰임새는 쓰는 곳, 말의 쓰임새는 쓰는 방법과 상황이에요.
explain_en: You say '쓰임새가 많다/적다/있다/없다' and '쓰임새를 찾다'. '용도' is the fixed purpose, while '쓰임새' is about how and where something actually gets used, and it sounds easier and softer. The '쓰임새' of money is where it is spent; of a word, how and in what situations it is used.

examples.en: When May comes, the scent of acacia flowers fills the air.
I picked acacia flowers and tried eating them.

examples.ko: 아카시아 나무 아래에서 벌들이 꿀을 모아요.
examples.en: Bees collect honey beneath the acacia tree.
Acacia honey is clear and sweet.
Acacias have bloomed fully along the road.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 아카시아 잎으로 가위바위보를 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I played rock-paper-scissors with acacia leaves.

explain: 한국에서 '아카시아'라고 부르는 나무는 식물 이름으로는 '아까시나무'예요. 하지만 일상에서는 '아카시아'가 훨씬 흔해요. 오월에 흰 꽃이 피고 '아카시아 꿀'로도 유명해요.
explain_en: The tree Koreans call '아카시아' is botanically '아까시나무', but in daily life '아카시아' is far more common. It has white flowers in May and is also famous for '아카시아 꿀' (acacia honey).

examples.en: Colorful balloons floated into the sky.

examples.ko: 오색 한복을 입은 아이들이 춤을 춰요.
examples.en: Children in colorful hanbok are dancing.
Multicolored autumn leaves dyed the mountain.
The fireworks painted the night sky in many colors.

examples.ko: 저녁 하늘에 오색 구름이 떠 있었어요.
examples.en: Colorful clouds floated in the evening sky.
The market was full of vegetables of every color.

explain: 원래는 파랑·노랑·빨강·하양·검정의 다섯 색이에요. 한국 전통에서는 '오방색'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 숫자 5보다 '여러 가지 화려한 색'이라는 느낌으로 써서 '오색 단풍', '오색찬란하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Originally it means the five colors blue, yellow, red, white and black, called '오방색' in Korean tradition. In daily use it feels like 'many splendid colors' rather than the number five, as in '오색 단풍' and '오색찬란하다'.

examples.en: I won the silver prize at the contest.
My younger sister won the silver prize at the drawing contest.
I got a culture gift certificate as the silver prize reward.

examples.ko: 아쉽게 금상은 못 탔지만 은상도 기뻐요.
examples.en: I missed the gold prize, but I'm happy with silver too.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 은상에 뽑혀서 박수를 받았어요.
examples.en: Our team was chosen for the silver prize and got applause.
This year's silver prize went to a new writer.

explain: 시상할 때는 '금상 → 은상 → 동상' 순서로 말해요. 올림픽 같은 스포츠에서는 '금메달/은메달'이라고 하고, 대회나 공모전의 상에는 '금상/은상'을 써요. '은상을 받다/타다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Prizes are named in the order '금상 → 은상 → 동상'. In sports like the Olympics, people say '금메달/은메달', while '금상/은상' is used for contest and competition awards. You say '은상을 받다/타다'.

examples.en: Birds fly freely through the sky.

examples.ko: 이 도서관에서는 책을 자유로이 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: In this library you can read books freely.
He expressed his thoughts freely.
The kids run and play freely on the playground.
I want to use my time freely.

examples.ko: 누구나 자유로이 의견을 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can freely offer an opinion.

explain: 말할 때는 '자유롭게'가 훨씬 흔하고, '자유로이'는 글 같은 느낌이 조금 있어요. 둘 다 '자유롭다'에서 온 부사예요. ㅂ 불규칙 형용사라서 '자유롭다'가 '자유로이'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: In speech '자유롭게' is much more common, while '자유로이' sounds a bit written. Both are adverbs from '자유롭다'. Because it is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, '자유롭다' turns into '자유로이'.
